decision: Per PROTOCOL section 3: both families failed, so the unquantized controls were completed, quantization loss was separated from probe failure, and the constrained ACS fitting branch is CLOSED. No Q was fitted on ACS. No third code family, no extra year, no relaxed threshold.

quantized_code_beats_H.reading: The 64-state pca32 code adds real residence capability over H alone, corrected.

unquantized_A_side_beats_J_on_residence.reading: The unquantized standardized A-side PCA32 view attains strictly LOWER residence loss than the same-host J channel, with adjusted one-sided upper bounds below zero under both weightings. The A-side inputs therefore carry residence signal beyond J's 16-coordinate auxiliary channel. This quantitatively contradicts the precursor's subsumption claim (PRECURSOR_CORRECTIONS.md C1, C2).

internal_consistency_check.note: exactly 0.00000 with zero SE because the zj family's unquantized view IS Z_J. This is an IDENTITY confirming the family is wired correctly, and per PRECURSOR_CORRECTIONS.md C3 it is NOT reported as evidence of anything and its zero variance is NOT precision.

name: Stage R representation screen (Section 6)

P1.outcome: REFUTED on both halves. Both families failed, AND pca32 was clearly the better of the two (deficit +0.00576 vs +0.01903 unweighted). My stated reason - that a J-derived code should preserve more of J - was wrong: Z_J is already a 16-dim compressed summary, so quantizing it to 64 states destroys proportionally more than quantizing the richer 32-dim input space.
P1.text: zj family passes the R screen; pca32 fails it

P2.outcome: CONFIRMED decisively: +0.0211 nats (pca32 k=64) and +0.0190 (zj k=64).
P2.text: H+raw beats H+T for both families, i.e. quantization costs measurable utility

screen_rule.kind: point-estimate scheduling rule, NOT a confidence non-inferiority claim

verdict: FAIL for both families at both resolutions
what_this_does_not_establish: NOT that no replacement can work. A different code family is unregistered tonight and was not tested.
NOT that useful information is absent - the opposite was measured: the unquantized view beats J.
NOT a statement about disclosure. No privacy constraint was applied and no Q was fitted on ACS, so nothing here bears on the utility/disclosure tradeoff.
NOT a population claim. Repeatedly used 2018 development pools; task-informed development throughout.

why_it_failed.diagnosis: Quantization, not probe failure. The unquantized view has NO deficit versus J - it is strictly better - while the 64-state code gives away 0.019 to 0.021 nats and the 256-state fallback gives away more still. At k=256 the one-hot block is 256 columns on 4539 fitting rows, so the fallback is additionally estimation-limited; at k=64 the binding loss is the coder itself.

quantization_cost_nats_unweighted.definition: (H+T deficit vs J) minus (H+raw deficit vs J); isolates the coder from the probe
